Belgium’s Chemicals Trade Remains Steady in Second Quarter

Belgium’s chemicals industry reported stable trade flows in the second quarter of 2024, with official figures indicating a slight year-on-year growth in both exports and imports, according to data released Thursday by the Belgian Trade Statistics Office.

Exports of chemicals and related products reached €17.2 billion for the quarter, up 2.1% from €16.9 billion in the same period last year. Imports also grew, totaling €15.8 billion, a 1.7% increase over the prior year. The figures reflect steady international demand amid broadly stable prices for key chemical compounds and intermediates.

“The chemicals sector continues to demonstrate resilience, supported by strong intra-EU trade and consistent demand from pharmaceutical and manufacturing clients,” said Annick Dervaux, head of economic analysis at the Federation of Belgian Chemical Industries. “While global logistics challenges have eased, our members are closely monitoring input costs, particularly for energy and specialty raw materials.”

Industry analysts highlighted continued robust shipments to neighboring Germany, France, and the Netherlands, as well as moderate growth in exports to the United States and Southeast Asia. “Belgium’s chemicals exporters benefit from well-developed infrastructure at Antwerp and Zeebrugge, which keeps throughput efficient and reliable,” observed Marc De Smet, senior analyst at Tradexis Consulting.

Employment across the industry remained stable at around 92,000 direct jobs, according to union figures. “Stable trade activity is positive for our members, who value predictability in order volumes,” said Katrien Boone, spokesperson for the United Chemical Workers Union.

Market participants report no major supply disruptions, trade policy changes, or logistical backlogs during the quarter. The sector’s performance aligns with broader trends in Belgian manufacturing, which has seen modest but steady growth in 2024.

The next release of industry data is scheduled for October, covering third-quarter developments. For now, stakeholders describe the outlook as “broadly stable,” with no significant disruptions anticipated.
